newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore jet/kerosene firms despite stock rise.
newsitem.headline: Singapore jet/kerosene firms despite stock rise.

text.p: Singapore gas oil fell on Thursday as weekly middle distillate stocks rose by 245,000 barrels to 8.7 million barrels, the highest level since September last year.

But jet/kerosene rose despite the higher stocks as majors bid the jet/gas oil spread on paper. November was talked firmer with deals reported at +$1.25 and +$1.15, compared to Wednesday's +$0.85 level. Traders said although some enquiries were made out of South Korea for the winter burning fuel, bids were not firm. In Singapore, only sellers were seen for November 100,000 barrel-cargoes, between $30.70-$30.30 a barrel fob.

Gas oil offers for 230,000 barrel-cargoes were lower at $30.60 for early November lifting. A buyer improved its bid from $29.80 to $30.10. Traders said the market was long with Indonesia expected to return to its normal monthly requirement of two million barrels in November after having increased its purchases in October due to Cilacap's 55,000 barrel-per-day visbreaker shutdown. But some traders said the outlook was less bearish with Mideast supplies tight while Chinese demand re-emerged. Bids for late October/early November cargoes were heard at $232-$234 a tonne on a cost-and-freight basis to South China. Sellers were only heard at $236.00.

Light disitllate stocks were down by 544,000 barrels to 5.407 million barrels. Prices remained unchanged in a lacklustre market although current high international prices prompted Taiwan to cancel its leaded reformate requirement for December. An official said it may consider re-issuing the tender should prices weaken. In the same tender, Taiwan bought award two leaded cargoes for late November and first half December at $25.90 a barrel.
